Reviewed full-K CMEM panel capacity: preserve selected panel shape and input reuse, request one or two slots, reduce actual slots for capacity or a single outer tile. Existing deterministic group shrink/bypass fallback remains. Both allocated slots count against the equal per-core no-borrow share. Serial mode may reserve two slots but does not use overlap.

Reviewed explicit non-preemptive shared HBM fill/export service, independent CMEM directional services, full-panel readiness before consumption and slot release only after its final CMEM read. Initial second-slot prefetch may delay the first export. Later refills run before the current export only if the whole fill fits; otherwise export runs first. This is a stated heuristic, not optimal hardware scheduling.

Reviewed isolated inner-block profiles: the body requires no HBM in tiled mode; final export is scheduled against outer fills. The first output drains outstanding HBM fill, all middle outputs can aggregate, and the last output determines CMEM lifetime. Existing K prefetch/shared VMEM behavior is unchanged. Row/column repeated-state jumps leave tail and lookahead boundaries explicit.

Six new scheduler tests cover a 176-cycle versus 192-cycle hand case with an 8-cycle HBM export wait, single-slot early release at cycle 63, 24 randomized tail/service/startup cases with explicit traces and resource/lifetime checks, capacity thresholds, billion-panel and two-dimensional tail aggregation, and invalid slot policies. Full workspace unittest suite passed 184 tests; source-audit and execution-contract focused checks passed 13 tests.

Reviewed remaining overlap boundaries in ARCHITECTURE: cross-output VMEM input prefetch, previous-C export versus next compute, partial-CMEM-fill consumption and per-MXU wave pipelining are not implemented. TSP simplified MEM concurrency: independent read/write budgets remain 320 B/cycle/slice. Retire mem_shared_bpc and preserve its complete previous evidence. TSP has 30 non-null parameters, 19 documented and 11 assumed; audit covers 108 active parameters, 68 documented and 40 assumed.

Standard and lite both encode 2150704873472 B/s for shared CMEM. Durable source audit retains version, offsets, hashes and values after scratch cleanup.

The dependency-constrained pipeline remains the only Ascend timing model. Misses have serial HBM-fetch/L2-fill/L2-read services, hits only L2-read. Fill/read share one L2 service, input/output share HBM; program-order input completion aligns logical LRU decisions with timing. Compute/output may overlap.

Docs state the whole-panel store-and-forward approximation and nonoptimal greedy arbitration. One buffer yields 42601 cycles versus 43588 with two; additional slots need not improve a greedy schedule. No cache-line/associativity/bank/NoC/DRAM-controller or cross-core cache model is claimed; estimates are not calibrated bounds.

TPU schema 7 migration adds execution.cmem_buffer_slots=1 or 2 and upgrades hardware to 8; report schema is 9. Legacy schema 7, missing/invalid slots and retired fields reject. Requested/effective mode and CMEM slots are disclosed. Console and JSON report outer-overlap savings relative to the previous outer-serial/inner-pipelined baseline.

README/ARCHITECTURE document the character dataflow, two-level buffering, independent CMEM directions, shared HBM arbitration, last-read slot release and first-fill/final-drain costs. One CMEM slot may still overlap a tail, while serial disables all overlap. Single-panel tiny has zero outer-overlap savings. Remaining overlap opportunities and public-evidence limits are explicit.

Native aggregates activation and partial-sum reads before max with writes. CIM uses separate mem_read and mem_write reservations; background LW still contends with other reads and stream_in. Dependencies, stream budgets, wave barriers and physical capacity remain. No 640 B/cycle single-direction service is introduced.

TSP hardware/report 7/7 and CIM 6/8 require execution.rules.mem_read_write=independent_assumed_conflict_free. Old schemas, combined-cap fields and missing/unsupported policies reject. Six new tests cover hand calculations, directional contention, background loads, missing services, migration and report disclosure.

36 saved GEMM comparisons preserve counts, action counts, memory and work views. 12 cases improve and 24 retain cycle counts. For M4/K640/N640 with one slice and 32 streams, native cycles change 1466 to 1439 and CIM 1502 to 1472. Default tiny remains 588/4307.

Existing numeric regressions and CLI acceptance expectations were updated for the new CMEM proxy; the complete integrated test/CLI result is recorded separately in run/acceptance.json. Concurrent architecture changes and their prior review are preserved.

No schema migration or new parameter is required for this reference-value refresh. README/ARCHITECTURE disclose both directional assumptions, exact software constants and current example cycles. Downloaded binaries/source and TPU scratch backups are disposable; durable provenance and tracked validation evidence remain.

A1: Ascend hardware schema 8 adds five explicit assumed, non-null Vector service parameters: shared per-core base=64 op/cycle, INT32 ADD and FP32 ADD/MUL cost=1, FP32 EXP cost=15, FP32 RSQRT cost=12. All 31 Ascend numeric parameters have values. Source audit entries and canonical configuration hash are synchronized.

Huawei Research June 2022 Table 5 (PDF p113) gives Ascend-Max vector width 256 bytes. 256/4=64 elements/group is geometry; one group/cycle is explicitly assumed, not inferred as documented or measured throughput. No independent SFU or additional inventory is introduced.

EXP and RSQRT adopt TSP algorithmic work conventions, not TSP native instruction timing or its 320 op/cycle budget. EXP costs range reduction 4 + degree-5 Horner work 10 + scale 1; RSQRT costs bit seed 2 + two 5-operation Newton iterations. Domain restrictions, no numerical execution and no accuracy guarantee are explicit.

Aggregate counts are mechanically recomputed from current audit entries. Prior source/code reviews remain history; this incremental review covers only Ascend and supporting documentation. Concurrent TPU-specific fingerprints are intentionally retained until their separate review. No silicon calibration or external sign-off is claimed.
A5: Ascend report schema 10 adds hardware_derived.vector_service and a console service summary. The API vector_service_cycles validates supported operation names and nonnegative integer scalar-element counts, sums rational weighted work and rounds once. Distinct operation rates share one budget. Changing inventory/core count/clock does not silently scale this fixed per-core cycle service.

Only active operations require their configured budget and costs. Unknown unused Vector services do not block GEMM; empty work returns zero, unsupported names still reject, and missing schema fields never fall back to geometry. Old schema 7 rejects with migration guidance. Retired generic FP32/SFU parameters stay retired.

Current GEMM keeps Cube/L0C accumulation and invokes no Vector service; no extra INT32 add is inserted. Standalone services omit transfers, reductions, conversions, dependency/issue/tail scheduling and fixed latency, so they are not complete Softmax/RMSNorm or native Exp/Rsqrt operator latencies. README and ARCHITECTURE include scope, source distinction, formula, API example and migration.

44 focused Ascend tests and 13 common audit/execution-contract tests passed. Eight before/after reports (four shapes in count/timing) exactly preserve counts, actions, memory, cache, stages, timing, strategy and boundary. Default GEMM remains 43588 cycles. Full-suite and CLI outcomes are recorded separately by verify_issue2.py.
